This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as concerning the child must indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. Applicable laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. Compliance must be given to all orders and instructions promulgated in connection with the new course of study issued December 1, 1915. The information as to public school facilities called for in the certificate of the Superintendent (third page hereof) must be given, and all superintendents are especially directed to exhaust every means to secure enrollment of Indian children in the State public schools, pursuant to instructions heretofore issued in this regard. Cushman Trades School Tacoma, Washington November 4, 1917 The decision of the girls and their officers is that Dora Rogers, Viola Rennels and Nancy Moses, shall be guarded closely by guards, who will march them to and from the dining hall etc. They shall be given extra work, Saturdays afternoons and Sundays, and all privileges taken from them. The guards shall be Cecelia Rankout, Rebecca Carpenter, and Lillian Whitman. The punishment of Nancy, Viola and Dora will extend until they can and will behave as they should, they will also eat their meals at a table at the middle of the dining hall. Signed: Capt. Mr. Charles Scherette, Meteor, Wash. Bushman School Tacoma, W.M. Hello Charlie, I am now going to write to you and tell you all about the things what I and Hannah have been doing here. I work in the kitchen and Hannah doesn't know where she works. I went to school this afternoon and the other outfit went this morning when you see me you will not recognize me and have nothing left of me but a head, legs, and arms. I have a bad cold. I seen Dewey Dean maybe you know him. I am going to try and get home. I don't like it here. Some of the girls run away at the first time and 3 and 4. But there is some gone yet. I am not going to try it because the punish hard here there arets 150 girls Eddie Ferguson is going home he is expelled. Tell mummie I said hello to her I do wish I was home I seen Elmer Durant I am in a hurry I got to got to supper I will write and tell you some more and might do better I think they will close the school because there is some kind of sickness sweeping back and forth. You know from good by Donah 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash. May 28, 1917 Mr. T. B. Wilson, Supt. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. My dear Mr. Wilson: I have your letter of the 20th ult. in which you approve of the request of Margaret McDonald or Rosalie H. Norden, as we have her on our records, and her cousin, Dora Noyes, to remain at your school during the summer vacation. I think the idea of their remaining there a good one and I am enclosing herewith checks in the sum of $15 for each of the girls to pay for any legitimate expenses they may find necessary to incur during their stay this summer. Very respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. AB/FS Please have these checks endorsed by the girls and the amounts placed to their credit on your books to be used for their benefit. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. June 4, 1917. Mr. J. M. Johnson, Supt., Colville Indian Agency, Nespelem, Washington. Dear Sir: Receipt is hereby acknowledged of your letter of May 28, inclosing a check each for Dora Noyes and Margaret McDonald or Rosalie H. Norden, for $15.00 each. This money will be placed to their credit and handled in the usual manner. Very respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Nov. 21, 1918. Mr. Pete Noyes, Pesch, Washington. Dear Mr. Noyes: I am returning herewith the money order for $5.00 which you sent to Dora. She has more than sufficient money at the office with the $30.00 sent her some time ago to come home on. When she wrote she was sick with the grippe and discouraged of course. She is now well and when I spoke to her about writing to go home, she told me she didn't want to go home. Don't you worry about Dora. We will take care of her the best we can and if she falls really sick, I will notify you promptly. Sincerely yours, Superintendent Peach Wash Nov 17 My Dear Daughter, I received your letters today was glad to hear from you and that you are well. There has been nobody died here yet, ever badly so well I have not heard a sneeze since you left there but I am going up there the first of the week and I will your aunt if you can stay there when you come back. I wish you could stay at school until next spring but of course if you have to come back I will send you some money to come home but I want you to see the Superintendent and I want you to know I am away and let me know. I am doing somehow. I want to get all the money I can before it freezes. I have not heard from your aunt but I guess they are all right now. Don't if you can stay there this winter. I would like it but of course if you are sick I don't want you to stay. I want you to come back so let me know soon. I have not sold all the cattle yet and have been short of money that is the reason I did not send you any but just as soon as I get Square with everybody. I will send you some every month so let me know as soon as you can about coming so I will make arrangements. From your Father P H write to Peach Wask DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Washington. December 16, 1916. Supt. T. B. Wilson, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Sir: I am enclosing herewith check No. 1911 in the sum of $25.00 on the account of Dora Noyes, which please place to her account. Very respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. Sm Enc Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. December 20, 1916. Mr. J. M. Johnson, Supt. Colville Agency, Nespelem, Washington. Dear Sir: I am in receipt of your letter of December 16 inclosing check No. 1911 in favor of Dora Noyes, for $25.00. This check has been handled in the usual manner. Very respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Sept. 5, 1918. Miss Dora Foyes, Lincoln, Wash. Dear Friend: Referring to your letter of March 21, 1918 written to your cousin here, in which you requested re-enrollment in this school, would advise that school opens today and actual classroom and industrial instruction begins September 9th. If you intend to return to school this year, I would advise you to come immediately and get an early start so that you may keep abreast with your classes. Awaiting either your reply or arrival, I am, Yours very truly, Superintendent Lincoln Park March 2018 My Dear Cousin, I am going to write you a letter in a hurry to tell you to ask Mr. Hammond if I can come over there to school now. I would be over there now but I thought he would not have me now until school started. But I am willing to go you asked him in a hurry. And write to me in Lincoln and tell me about it in a hurry. Oh you don't know how glad I am to go. The place here is dry now and supposed to be fine weather. But tonight it is little rainy. I came here last night with papa. I can't tell you any more. I am in a hurry. I will tell you when I get there. Tell Edith I said hello to her. I guess you don't think this is my writing. But it is I learned a letter. I suppose you will be glad to see my old face again don't you? Not very long from now if you hurry and talked well. Good By from Dora Fay Lincoln Wa Ans soon please 5-297 e LAUNDERING.
